title: How to Migrate Without Losing Process History
summary: See how to migrate from a Kanban tool to a full process management system without losing history or data.
body_markdown:
It's possible to **migrate without losing process history** by exporting data from the current tool and importing it into a system that recognizes the structure automatically, keeping records, dates, and each card's history intact. In **Jestor** , this import generates relational tables ready for automation.


Fear of losing history is the main reason a migration stalls, even when the current tool no longer fits the process.


That fear makes sense when migrating means recreating everything manually, card by card. It makes less sense when the new tool can actually import what already exists.


## What Stalls a Migration Without Planning


- Fear of losing cards, comments, or creation dates during the switch
- No mapping of which fields exist today and where they should go
- No test period before migrating the whole team at once
- No plan for processes still in progress at the moment of the switch


## How to Migrate While Preserving History


1. Export data from the current tool, including dates, statuses, and filled-in fields
2. Import the data into the new system and check whether each field was recognized correctly
3. Migrate one specific process first, not the whole operation at once
4. Keep both systems active for a short period, until you confirm nothing was left out
5. Only deactivate the old tool after validating that the migrated history is complete


Stage Main thing to watch


Export Include dates, statuses, and comments, not just the main fields


Import Check whether each column was recognized as the right data type


Pilot Migrate one process before migrating all of them at once


Transition Keep both systems active until the full history is validated


## Why Migrating to Jestor Preserves History


- The import automatically recognizes columns, data types, and relationships between tables
- Every record keeps a change history, visible right inside the card
- A **trash bin** recovers records deleted by mistake during the transition
- The **Jestor** team helps with initial setup at no charge, lowering the risk of errors during migration


## Frequently asked questions


**Is it possible to lose data during migration?** The risk exists in any migration; validating the import before deactivating the old system reduces that risk.


**Do I need to migrate every process at once?** No, migrating one process at a time, starting with a pilot, tends to be safer; see more at[jestor.com](https://www.jestor.com/?ref=blog.jestor.com) .


**Are comments and attachments also preserved?** It depends on the export format available in the source tool; it's best to confirm before migrating.


**Can a record deleted by mistake be recovered after migration?** Yes, **Jestor** 's trash bin lets you recover records and fields deleted by accident.


In the end, being able to **migrate without losing process history** depends more on planning than on the tool chosen.
